recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Revisit only if FHIR-I and Security decide to split the current single implementer safety checklist into separate authoritative checklists, which would require coordinated edits to source/safety.html and the safety-entries CodeSystem.
issue_request: FHIR-16528 was Published/Persuasive with Modification. It asked that the clinical safety page reference the security page and avoid maintaining a separate duplicate security/privacy checklist; the accepted modification approved the proposed checklist in principle while Grahame worked with Security editors to fine tune it.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied by 68f6cca29ae4d06f089f338982a2b98269e1a48a, which rewrote source/safety.html into an Implementer's Safety CheckList, stated that safety is interpreted loosely to include security and privacy, and added privacy/security checklist sections with links into security/privacy content.
additional_context: Current source/safety.html still states that the checklist covers security/privacy issues, exposes the checklist as the safety-entries CodeSystem, and links security entries to source/security.html and related security/privacy pages. Current source/security.html remains the dedicated FHIR Security page. The December 2018 Zulip thread shows the requested fine tuning with Security participants before the reconciled page was posted for comment; later safety checklist commits maintain the checklist model rather than reversing it.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit. No source change is needed because removing the security/privacy items or replacing them with only a generic pointer would undo the modified decision and later checklist maintenance, while adding another generic pointer would be redundant with existing item-level links.
